elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-provided services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires HDI to defend the Company and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the Site or HDI-provided services, software, or materials infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-provided services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires HDI to indemnify the Company and its affiliates against such claims and resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The introductory defense obligation applies to third-party claims arising out of “HDI's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The introductory indemnification obligation applies to third-party claims and resulting losses arising out of “HDI's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation covers third-party claims arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Confidential Information caused by HDI.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation covers third-party claims and resulting losses arising from unauthorized access to or disclosure of the Company's data or Confidential Information caused by HDI.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising out of HDI's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers third-party claims and resulting losses arising out of HDI's gross negligence.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation expressly covers third-party claims arising out of HDI's “willful misconduct,” an equivalent spelling of wilful misconduct.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers third-party claims and resulting losses arising out of HDI's willful misconduct.

elements.element: Customer must provide notice of an indemnified claim to Vendor.
elements.evidence: The Company must “promptly notify HDI of any such claim.”

elements.element: Vendor must be permitted to control the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The Company must “permit HDI to control the defense thereof.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: The Company must “provide reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: The supplied operative language imposes no indemnity obligation on the Company; therefore, the condition for restricting a Customer indemnity is demonstrably absent, and no broader Customer indemnity is created.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that Vendor-provided services or deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section (c) requires HDI to indemnify the Company against third-party claims alleging infringement or misappropriation by the Site or HDI-provided services, software, or materials.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by the Company appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from combinations with items not provided or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from compliance with Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for compliance with Company specifications appears. The exclusion for Company-provided Content is not an equivalent specifications exclusion.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected item.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no procure-right remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to modify the affected item so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For covered IP infringement, Vendor must have or provide a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The operative language contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to 3× annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section (c) contains no liability cap or reference to a cap equal to three times annual fees.

result.reason: The redline adds the complete preferred Vendor defense-and-indemnity package, including all specified triggers, beneficiaries, and notice/control/cooperation procedures, without creating an overbroad Customer indemnity or changing the existing Globix provision. It does not independently satisfy the fallback because the specified IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The drafting is substantively strong, with only a minor grammatical issue in “the Site or any services, software or materials ... infringes,” which should use “infringe.”
